name: OMathDelim
description: Represents a delimiter object, consisting of opening and closing delimiters (such as parentheses, braces, brackets, or vertical bars), and one or more elements contained inside the delimiters.

properties.name: Application
properties.description: Returns an Application object that represents the Microsoft Word application.

properties.name: Creator
properties.description: Returns a 32-bit integer that indicates the application in which the add-in was created. Read-only Long.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Returns an Object that represents the parent object of the specified OMathDelim object.

properties.name: E
properties.description: Returns an OMathArgs object that represents the list of arguments for the specified equation object. Read-only.

properties.name: BegChar
properties.description: Returns or sets an Integer that represents the beginning delimiter character in a delimiter object. Read/write.

properties.name: SepChar
properties.description: Returns or sets an Integer that represents the separator character in a delimiter object when the delimiter object contains two or more arguments. Read/write.

properties.name: EndChar
properties.description: Returns or sets an Integer that represents the ending delimiter character in a delimiter object. Read/write.

properties.name: Grow
properties.description: Returns or sets a Boolean that represents whether delimiter characters grow to the full height of the arguments that they contain. Read/write.

properties.name: Shape
properties.description: Returns or sets a WdOMathShapeType constant that represents the appearance of delimiters (for example, parentheses, braces, and brackets) in relationship to the content that they surround. Read/write.

properties.name: NoLeftChar
properties.description: Returns or sets a Boolean that represents whether to hide the opening delimiter in a delimiter object. Read/write.

properties.name: NoRightChar
properties.description: Returns or sets a Boolean that represents whether to hide the closing delimiter in a delimiter object. Read/write.
